title: Swimming Champion Archie Goodburn to Deliver Rugby Match Ball in Front of 60,000 Fans
summary:
Archie Goodburn is a champion swimmer from Edinburgh, Scotland. On Sunday, November 15, he will have a special job at a rugby game. He will carry the match ball onto the field before Scotland plays Australia at Murrayfield, in front of more than 60,000 fans.

Goodburn, who is 25, is a British champion and a European bronze medallist. He also holds the Scottish record for the 50-metre breaststroke. In 2024, doctors found that he had a rare brain tumour. After surgery, he worked hard and returned to competitive swimming. Now he also campaigns for better brain cancer treatment and research, and he has taken his campaign to Prime Minister Andy Burnham and to Scotland's First Minister, John Swinney. Fans at the game can also donate to two brain cancer charities.

Rugby is not new to him. He once played rugby at school, and at age 12 he sang a solo in front of 10,000 people. 'This means the absolute world to me,' he said.
why_it_matters: It shows that even after a serious illness, you can work hard, get back to doing what you love, and use your story to help other people.
